sanskrit_shloka:
अष्टावक्र उवाच ॥
आचक्ष्व श‍ृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः ।
तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥ १६-१॥
translation: Aṣṭāvakra said: O dear one, speak of or listen to the many śāstras in countless ways; yet you will not find inner peace unless everything is forgotten.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Aṣṭāvakra said: O dear one, speak of or listen to the many śāstras in countless ways; yet you will not find inner peace unless everything is forgotten.

commentary_faqs.question: Why does Ashtavakra say we must "forget everything"?
commentary_faqs.answer: It refers to letting go of intellectual constructs, labels, and the ego's identification with knowledge, which block the direct experience of the Self.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the "champion of idleness" mentioned in Verse 4?
commentary_faqs.answer: It describes a state of total non-doing where one is so established in the Self that even the slightest mental effort or movement of dualistic thought is seen as unnecessary.

sanskrit_shloka:
भोगं कर्म समाधिं वा कुरु विज्ञ तथापि ते ।
चित्तं निरस्तसर्वाशमत्यर्थं रोचयिष्यति ॥ १६-२॥
translation: Whether you pursue enjoyment, action, or samādhi, O wise one, your mind will be utterly pleased only when it is stripped of every hope and desire.

translations.author: English Translation

sanskrit_shloka:

अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥ १६-३॥
translation: All suffer through effort, yet no one understands this. By this very teaching, the blessed one attains supreme repose—liberation.

sanskrit_shloka:
व्यापारे खिद्यते यस्तु निमेषोन्मेषयोरपि ।
तस्यालस्य धुरीणस्य सुखं नान्यस्य कस्यचित् ॥ १६-४॥
translation: One who is wearied even by the closing and opening of the eyes is the master of sacred idleness, of effortlessness; true happiness belongs to him alone, to no one else.

sanskrit_shloka:
इदं कृतमिदं नेति द्वन्द्वैर्मुक्तं यदा मनः ।
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु निरपेक्षं तदा भवेत् ॥ १६-५॥
translation: When the mind is freed from the dualities of “this is done” and “this is not done,” and becomes indifferent to dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, then it is truly free.

sanskrit_shloka:
विरक्तो विषयद्वेष्टा रागी विषयलोलुपः ।
ग्रहमोक्षविहीनस्तु न विरक्तो न रागवान् ॥ १६-६॥
translation: The dispassionate one spurns the objects of the senses; the attached one craves them greedily. But one free from grasping and release is neither dispassionate nor attached.

sanskrit_shloka:

translation: So long as desire lives, the notions of rejecting and accepting sustain the sprout of the tree of saṃsāra; in the state beyond discrimination, they vanish.

sanskrit_shloka:

translation: In activity attachment arises; in withdrawal, indeed, aversion. The wise one, beyond the pairs of opposites, remains established just so, like a child.

translation: The attached person wishes to abandon saṃsāra in order to escape suffering. But the one free from attachment and sorrow does not grieve, even within it.
